cohort: 592 women with a previous cesarean delivery who gave birth at the same hospital between January 2014 and December 2019
finding: There were no significant differences in the risks of adverse perinatal outcomes or successful vaginal birth between interpregnancy intervals of <18 months, 18-60 months, and >60 months after cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Researchers found that, after caesarean delivery, interpregnancy intervals shorter than 18 months and longer than 60 months did not significantly impact successful vaginal birth compared with interpregnancy intervals of 18-60 months.
